newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis wound 24 Palestinians in Hebron protests.
newsitem.headline: Israelis wound 24 Palestinians in Hebron protests.

text.p: Israeli troops shot and wounded at least 24 Palestinians, one critically, on Friday while fighting protesters who hurled fire bombs and stones at them in the streets of Hebron, witnesses said.
An Israeli army spokeswoman said two paramilitary border policemen were lightly wounded in the West Bank flashpoint town, one by a stone and the other by a firebomb.

Witnesses said masked Arabs flung scores of petrol bombs and some home-made explosive charges at Israeli soldiers who fired live ammunition and rubber-coated metal bullets from rooftops and from behind barricades along Shallaleh street, which divides Hebron into Israeli and PLO-controlled sections.

Medics at a Palestinian field clinic set up behind the line of clashes said they evacuated at least 24 people wounded by live ammunition or knocked down by the rubber bullets. Two teenagers were in serious condition after being hit in the head.

"We are trying to relieve the pressure from the hospitals," said Dr Rateb Zaitoun at the field clinic, erected at the courtyard of a local petrol station. He said a number of the victims were hit with live ammunition.
One of the wounded was Reuters photographer Rula Halawani, who was hit in the leg by a rubber bullet, witnesses said.
Major-General Uzi Dayan, commander of Israel's central region, which includes the West Bank, said troops were using force because Palestinian police were refusing to intervene.

"The Palestinian police is not doing its job here and under such circumstances we are doing the job and as you know today more than 15 Palestinians from the rioters were injured and are hospitalised," Dayan told reporters.
"We strike in a way that the rioters themselves will be hurt," he said.

Demonstrators challenged Israeli soldiers to face them without guns. At one point, they sent Israeli officers scurrying for shelter when youths hurled a home-made bomb at the courtyard of al-Yaacoubia school, where copies of the Moslem holy Koran were desecrated earlier this week.

An Israeli army spokeswoman said no soldiers were hurt in the explosion. But she said one soldier was lightly injured from a fire bomb thrown near by and a second soldier was in light to moderate condition after being hit with a stone. Both soldiers were taken to hospital for treatment, she said.

Hebron has been a scene of almost daily unrest since a Jewish woman plastered storefronts with anti-Moslem posters depicting the Moslem Prophet Mohammad as a pig two weeks ago. Israel-PLO peace talks have been frozen for four months.

Religous feelings were further inflamed when Palestinians found Yaacoubia school ransacked and four copies of the Koran torn up. Palestinians charged Israeli soldiers desecrated the holy books but the Israeli army denied the charge.
The clashes began on Friday when five masked youths burned two Israeli flags while others attacked a group of soldiers holed up inside the school with stones.

Some of the demonstrators used slingshots. Witnesses said more than 130 petrol bombs were thrown at soldiers, setting the stone-strewn road between the embattled groups on fire. They said two explosions were heard, apparently from homemade bombs.

Israel handed over most of Hebron, home to more than 100,000 Palestinians, to the PLO in January under a self-rule deal but kept troops behind to guard some 400 Jewish settlers living or studying in the heart of the old city.

Israeli troops have ringed the city with checkpoints, turning back Palestinians from nearby villages. The siege, described by Israel as necessary for security, has hurt the economy of the town which depends on trade with Palestinians outside Hebron.
